# Digivine API


## Testing and Exploring

### Configuration

Possible using a `conf.toml` in $PWD or environment variables, see `conf_default.toml` for entries.

### Test-running the Project

Run `docker-compose build` to build the project and `docker-compose up` to run the server along with a database backend.
Then a webserver will run under http://localhost:8080/ and you find:

* http://localhost:8080/api/<VERSION> the api
* http://localhost:8080/doc/ the documentation generated by openapi

### Using the API

Send a request by providing the api version, path, and `api-token` parameter, e.g.:

GET http://localhost:8080/api/v0.2/ero?api-token=all 


## Extending the API

Say you want to add a new data endpoint, say for "Lego" data. Then you need to do the following:

- extend the OpenAPI definition `./openapi`
- regenerate the server `cd libs ; ./generate_server.sh`
- add backend code in `libs/lego` (this is the code used for retreiving and manipulating data stored in a database)
- connect backend code in `Cargo.toml`
- add glue logic for json api and backend in `src/`

## Locally Generating OpenAPI Documentation

For generating the documentation into `out/html`, run this command:

```
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/local" openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate \
    -i /local/openapi/main.yaml \
    -g html \
    -o /local/out/html
```

Instead of `html` you can pass different generators after the `-g` flag, see [this list](https://openapi-generator.tech/docs/generators#documentation-generators).
